body: c1 lead returned SHIPPED. PR https://github.com/SatanshuMishra/logbook/pull/202, branch fix/close-releases-pointer, commit bd0a9c53974f6cb989ae40a893a20307120c6708. Design recorded as 01M1TVNXQEFNJ6PGG3D6R1GCD2.U+000AU+000AChange: close_thread.ts gains a layoutFor resolution and a releasePointerIfOwned call placed after store.commit succeeds. Ordering is load-bearing — released earlier, a failed close would strand the session, because park_thread carrying an outcome would then refuse with "no thread is currently marked as being worked" and report the outcome text as not stored.U+000AU+000ANew test/spawn/close.test.ts, four cases. RED on parent 4458ba76 with exit 1 and the first three failing: the two release cases found the pointer object where null was expected, and the park case matched thread A's id inside a notTheWorkedThreadRefusal. The fourth case, the anti-steal guard asserting a pointer naming another thread is left alone, passed on the parent by design and is not a reproduction. Inertness mutation: deleting only the releasePointerIfOwned line reproduced exit 1 with the same three failures; restoring it returned exit 0 with four passing, and the guard case passed with the line removed, confirming it never depended on the fix.U+000AU+000AOne pre-existing test was amended rather than weakened. test/spawn/resume.test.ts:952, park.releases-the-pointer-when-the-thread-is-already-terminal, had been reaching park_thread's terminal branch by relying on close leaving the pointer behind. It now captures the pointer file's bytes after resume_thread and writes them back after the close, so it still drives that branch and would still catch a regression in it.U+000AU+000AReceipts: npm test exit 0 at 818 passed 0 failed 0 skipped; npm run typecheck exit 0 no diagnostics; targeted runs of resume.test.ts 29 passed, lifecycle.test.ts 22 passed, contract/write-tools-ignore-the-pointer 2 passed, contract/continuity-rule-census 4 passed.U+000AU+000ANot verified, and carried as such in the PR body: behaviour inside a live Claude Code session was not run, because this repo is the dogfooded plugin and working-tree edits do not reach the running MCP server until reinstall and restart; and a real two-session concurrent race was not run, so the cross-session release argument is reasoned through code rather than executed.U+000AU+000Ac1 stays OPEN rather than being marked done. The behaviour is true on the branch, not on main, and merge is human-gated.U+000AU+000ACollision to watch: PR 202 also touches docs/rules/continuity-ledger.md at 96-98, adding close_thread to the pointer lifecycle. The parallel documentation lead is editing the same file at 126-127 on its own branch off the same parent. Different sections, so git should auto-merge, but whichever lands second may need a merge commit.
